name: Apple tart
description: The best homemade tart that brings back childhood memories every time!

name: Arepa burgers
description: Delicious and simple, great alternative burger!
instructions: I typically make this from frozen arepas and defrost them in an air fryer. If you don’t have an air fryer you can take them out of the freezer sooner.
On a low medium heat on the hob slowly heat your frying pan. When it’s hot add the arepas.
On another ring heat a sauté pan on a low medium heat and ad the burger patties. Cover them with a lid.
After about 10-15 minutes check the arepas. They should be browned on the side facing the heat, just be careful as if they are not cooked they can stick. Once you’re happy flip them.
Do the same with the burger patties. If they are cooking too slowly increase the heat to a medium heat. The juice in the pan is good and will help to create a better burger.
When you’re happy the burger is almost cooked, take the lid off and clean the pan with the patties. Turn off the heat.
Take your tomato sauce from the fridge and to heat it put a dollop on each patty. Then add the cheese slices and put the lid back on to just melt the cheese.
Prepare your greens and onion.
When your arepas are done put them on a plate and add the greens on the bottom arepa ‘bun’. Then add the burger patty with tomato sauce and cheese. Top with your onion and place the top arepa bun.
Enjoy!

name: Arepas
description: So versatile and delicious! Great for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

name: Bagels
description: A delicious and chewy bagel that is perfect for breakfast or a snack. Enjoy with your favourite toppings!
aside: 💡 A strong mixer like a KitchenAid Pro (not available outside of the US) as a weaker one may break with the kneading. If you are uncertain do this by hand.
ingredients: 530 ml / 2¼ cups lukewarm water at 40 - 43 C (105 - 110 F)
2 tblsp barley malt syrup (can be substituted with molasses if required)
9 g / ¼ oz dry yeast (about 2¼ teaspoons)
6 ml / ¼ cup barley malt syrup, plus more as needed
30 g / 2 oz each sesame seeds, poppy seeds, caraway seeds, dried minced garlic, dried minced onion and/or flaky salt (optional)
instructions: Dissolve the barley malt in 200ml of the warm water and add the yeast. Hand whisk until all ingredients are incorporated and leave to rest until the top is full of foam.
Add the yeast and barley mixture to the rest of the water.

Put flour and salt into a strong mixer (see next step if you do not have a strong mixer), using the dough hook turn the mixer on and slowly add the yeasty liquid. Leave to mix on a low speed for min 10 mins.
(By hand method): Put flour into a large bowl and slowly mix in the yeasty liquid mixing by hand until the mixture is shaggy. Turn out onto floured surface and knead for a minimum of 15 minutes.
The mixture is ready when it is very elastic and have a little stickiness to it, but not so much that it sticks to your hands. This creates the chewy texture in a bagel.
### First proofing
Leave the mixture to rest in a bowl covered with a damp towel for the minimum of 2 hours and the mixture has doubled in size. You can leave it for up to 4 hours if the temperature isn't too hot.
### Shaping
Line two large rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper, brush lightly with oil and set aside.
💡 It is important to lightly oil the parchment paper here or the bagels will stick to it and ruin the shape later.
Take the mixture out and punch it on an unfloured surface. Divide it into 12 equal portions, usually about 115 g / 4 oz. (You can make this a bakers dozen of 13 if you wish for smaller bagels.)
Preshape the pieces into tight balls like you are making bread for a baneton, turning seam side down and tighten each ball.
Then cover with a damp towel and leave for 5 minutes to rest.
Working one piece at a time, roll out a ball on the surface into a 22 cm / 9 inch long snake.
Apply some pressure at each end of the snake and wrap the ends by 3 - 5 cm / 1 - 2 inches along the sides of your hand.
Roll the dough along the join to seal together the two ends. Then slip the ring of dough off your hand and stretch it out to be evenly on your baking sheet.
### Final proof
When all bagels have been formed cover them with damp towls or beeswax paper and leave them to proof at room temperature for about 1 hour and then put them in the fridge for the final proofing stage.
After 4 - 24 hours take them out of the fridge. If the bagels are not after rising to the desired size leave in room temparture for another 1 - 2 hours.
### Boiling and baking
💡 Prepare your work surface before you start boiling anything. Have a wire rack next to the dutch oven and plates with toppings as required next to that.
Turn the oven on at 225°C / 450°F.
Half fill a dutch oven with water and bring it to the boil. Whisk in the barley malt and baking soda in the water and bring to the boil. Scoop off any scum that formed.
Once boiling lower to keep simmering and add in 2 - 3 bagels.
Cook for 1 min and then turn over at 30 seconds.
![bagels-boiling.png](bagels-boiling.png)
Take out and place on the wire rack, then add the next bagels.
Using your hands take the bagels from the wire rack and put them in the desired plate to cover them in topping.
Place the covered bagel on the tray with the parchment paper.
![bagels-pre-bake.png]/bagels-pre-bake.png)
Bake the bagels for 20 - 25 mins, turning them over at 10 minuets.
Eat and enjoy!
💡 Bagels keep great in the freezer, I would recommend to slice them and then take them out when needed popping the into a toaster before eating!

name: Banana & chocolate cake
description: A staple, because it is the best banana and chocolate cake ever! It is so moist and delicious.
ingredients: 4.5 tsp baking powder / 1.5 tsp baking soda
instructions: Put the chocolate in a bain-marie on the stove to melt the chocolate
Preheat the oven to 180°C / 350°F
Mix the coconut oil, flavourings, sugar and slowly beat in the eggs
Add flour, baking flour, and cocoa slowly
Pour into prepared cake tin or bread tin
Bake in the oven for ~ 30 - 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Great served with crème fresh
Can be frozen

name: Bauernbrot
description: True to the german form, this is a hearty bread that is great for sandwiches or just with butter and sausage.

name: Bechamel sauce
description: A simple staple, every cook should master.
ingredients: 125g cheese (optional - whatever your recipe calls for)
1/2 tsp nutmeg (optional - a must in musaka)
instructions: On a low medium heat melt the butter.
Slowly add the flour and mix quickly and remove from the heat.
Slowly add in the milk; when it gets to a consistencly you can use the wisk, do so.
Return to a high heat and keep whisking until it thickens.

name: Beef bresaola
description: Find a recipe to make this. We had it as kangaroo in Clare Valley.

name: Bologenese
ingredients: 6 cloves of garlic (ajust to taste - I can go to a whole head)
1/2 cup/125ml of red wine (and now you can have a glass for yourself)
8 - 10 fresh tomatoes (or use [Garlic Roast Tomatoes ](Garlic%20Roast%20Tomatoes%20b24526b7e2cc426abc64abbcb59e0f5b.md) from frozen) (if you have nothing else a large tim of tomatoes is fine too
instructions: Fry the crushed garlic on a low to medium heat in the frying pan. When fragrant add the onions. Keep an eye on them stirring occasionally until they are translucent and a little bit caramel like.
Add meat and increase the temperature to a medium heat. Quickly scear the meat.
When it is as hot as it will get add the red wine. Stir and wait until the alcohol has burnt off.
Add the tomatoes and carrot.
Bring to a simmer, stir and return to low heat and leave simmering on the hob for ~45 mins, stiring occasionally.

name: Brine
description: The key to making succulent meat.
instructions: Heat water and dissolve salt (and spices if using) into it

name: Buffalo Hot Sauce
description: The best way to enjoy chicken wings! This is a simple recipe that is easy to make and delicious.
instructions: Trial ingredients which the largest quantity first. Blend all together and taste.

name: Carrot and Courgette cake
description: One of the best, healthy and easiest cakes to make. It is so moist and delicious.

name: Chestnut Burger Patty
description: A great alternative to meat, for that vego moment.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a frying pan on high.
Add the mushrooms and continue stirring regularly until browned.
Turn heat down to medium, add the onion and chives. Sauté for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the garlic, soy sauce and chestnuts. Sauté for a further minute, stirring.
Turn off the heat and allow it to cool slightly.
Place contents into a food processor. Season with salt and pepper, then process until mixture comes together but still has a slightly coarse texture.
Form the mixture into patties approximately 2cm thick. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until firm.
Heat frying pan and add the remaining olive oil.
Cook patties for 5-7 minutes on one side then flip for a further 5-7 minutes on the other side, or until cooked through and browned on the outside.

name: Chocolate bubka
aside: 💬 I have not made this, likely will want to reduce sugar.
instructions: *Make the dough:* Combine the flour, sugar, yeast and zest in

the bottom of the bowl of a stand mixer. Add eggs and 1/2 cup water, mixing with the dough hook until it comes together; this may take a couple minutes. It’s okay if it’s on the dry side, but if it doesn’t come together at all, add extra water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough forms a mass. With the mixer on low, add the salt, then the butter, a spoonful at a time, mixing until it’s incorporated into the dough.
Then, mix on medium speed for 10 minutes until dough is

completely smooth; you’ll need to scrape the bowl down a few times. I usually found that after 10 minutes, the dough began to pull away from the sides of the bowl. If it doesn’t, you can add 1 tablespoon extra flour to help this along.

Coat a large bowl with oil (or scrape the dough out onto a counter and oil this one) and place dough inside, cover with plastic and refrigerate. Leave in fridge for at least half a day, preferably overnight. [Dough will not fully double, so don’t fret if it doesn’t look like it grew by more than half.]
[To make this on the same day, cool in fridge before next step.]
*Make filling:* Melt butter and chocolate together until smooth.
Stir in powdered sugar and cocoa; mixture should form a spreadable paste. Add cinnamon, if desired. [If you’re wondering what happened to the pecans and granulated sugar, see my third note below.]

*Assemble loaves:* Coat two 9-by-4-inch (2 1/4 or 1kg) loaf pans with oil or butter, and line the bottom of each with a rectangle of parchment paper. Take half of dough from fridge (leave the other half chilled). Roll out on a well-floured counter to about a 10-inch width (the side closest to you) and as long in length (away from you) as you can when rolling it thin, likely 10 to 12 inches.

Spread half of chocolate mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1/2-inch border all around. Brush the end farthest away from you with water. Roll the dough up with the filling into a long, tight cigar. Seal the dampened end onto the log. I found that transferring the log to a lightly floured baking tray in the freezer for 10 to 15 minutes made it much, much easier to cut cleanly in half. Repeat with second dough.
Trim last 1/2-inch off each end of log. Gently cut the log in half
lenghtwise and lay them next to each other on the counter, cut sides up.
Pinch the top ends gently together. Lift one side over the next,

forming a twist and trying to keep the cut sides facing out (because they’re pretty). Don’t worry if this step makes a mess, just transfer the twist as best as you can into the prepared loaf pan. In one batch, mine was long enough to “S” inside the pan and I nested the trimmed ends of the log in the openings. Even if you don’t (and choose to bake them
separately in a little pan, as I did in other batches), the dough will fill in any gaps by the time it’s done rising and baking, so don’t worry.
Cover with a damp tea towel and leave to rise another 1 to 1 1/2 hours at room temperature. Repeat process with second loaf.
*Bake and finish cakes:* Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Remove

towels, place each loaf on the middle rack of your oven. Bake for 30 minutes, but there’s no harm in checking for doneness at 25 minutes. A skewer inserted into an underbaked babka will feel stretchy/rubbery inside and may come back with dough on it. When fully baked, you’ll feel almost no resistance.
If your babka needs more time, put it back, 5 minutes at a time then re-test. If it browns too quickly, you can cover it with foil.

While babkas are baking, make syrup: Bring sugar and water to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and set aside to cool somewhat. As soon as the babkas leave the oven, brush the syrup all over each. It will seem like too much, but will taste just right — glossy and moist. Let cool about halfway in pan, then transfer to a cooling rack to cool the rest of the way before eating (an adorable suggestion from Ottolenghi — don’t worry, we know you’re going to eat it warm).
*Do ahead:* Babkas keep for a few days at room temperature. Longer, I’d freeze them. They freeze and defrost really well.

name: Chocolate chip cookies 🍪
instructions: Beat butter and sugar till pale and creamy
Add eggs
Add flour, baking powder, cocoa
Add chocolate chips
Bake at 150°C fan forced for 20-25 mins if using 2 tbsp per cookie

name: Chocolate strawberries
instructions: Melt chocolate in water bath.
Dip strawberries in melted chocolate and let cool on parchment paper.

name: Cranberry sauce
instructions: Boil cranberries with water, half covering berries in pot. Add sugar to taste.

name: Egg custard
ingredients: 50g sugar (optional and not used in Xmas Trifle)
instructions: Beat the egg yolks.
Heat milk in bain-marie, being careful not to bring to the boil.
Pour heated milk over the eggs.
Stir on a gentle heat until it thickens.
Add vanilla extract.

name: Eggnog
aside: 💡Chef’s note: I reduced the sugar to 1/3. Alcohol could be 1 cup easily.
ingredients: 1 1/5 cups bourbon, rum, Cognac, or a mix (optional)
💡 Alcohol is required for aging the eggnog. It can be reduced to 1/2 cup or omitted altogether if not aging the eggnog.
instructions: Separate the eggs - when aging the eggnog you may be best to freeze the whites for later.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar until creamy.
Slowly whisk in the milk, cream and alcohol.
If aging store in the fridge for minimum 4 weeks. [Note to self: play with this]
Just before serving whisk the egg whites (remember to defrost them beforehand if aging).
Fold egg whites into eggnog mixture. (This lightens it and makes it even more creamy.)

name: Eggplant with Miso
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C / 360°F.
Lightly score the surface of the eggplant with the point of a sharp knife and then brush the surface very lightly with sesame oil.
In a bowl, combine all of the remaining ingredients, except the sesame seeds, stirring until smooth.

Preheat a frypan to high and spray with a little oil. Cook the eggplant for about 2 minutes until starting to colour. Flip each piece and continue cooking until both sides are nicely coloured and cooked.
Then remove from pan onto a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Spoon the miso mixture onto each one.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and place in the oven and cook until the miso starts to bubble.
Serve with white rice.

name: Espresso martini
instructions: Shake and serve

name: Fruit salad
instructions: Dissolve sugar in water.
Add lemon juice and rind of the lemon.
Mix in chopped fruit.

name: Garden salad
ingredients: Bunch of fresh mixed salad greens: roquette, lettuce, mustard greens, beetroot  leaves all are good ones.
Fresh herbs: basil, cilantro/corriander leaves, oregano etc are all good, whatever is in the garden
Dried herbs: whatever you have in the pantry that needs using, get fancy if you want
Edible flowers: nasturtiums, sunflowers, so many flowers are edible do your research
Vinegar: a wine is always good, so too is cider, just something fresh
instructions: Add dried herbs to a dash of vinegar and another dash of oil. Leave to sit for a minimum of 15 minutes. If you can leave it overnight that always works.
Pluck off all leaves from the salad greens. Chop up the remaining stalks finely and add to the leaves.
Finely chop the herbs, mixing them with the dried ones and the greens.
Add all remaining ingredients together, adding more vinegar and oil if needed.

name: Gin and tonic cake
description: See URL to try and then document

name: Granny Little’s Chocolate Mousse
instructions: Melt chocolate in water bath.
Separate egg, whisk yolk.
Add sugar, chocolate, vanilla and brandy.
Add in soft butter.
Whisk egg white and fold into the mix.
Leave to set in the fridge.

name: Hair pomade
description: Recipe variations: Creamy and light (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/Creamy%20and%20light%203e1eff326f6546709b99aa9e6957c3da.md), ChatGPT Idea (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/ChatGPT%20Idea%201868f15790cc80eeb150f1bcde72cadf.md)
ingredients: 1 part coconut oil (can try other oils too)
instructions: Melt the beeswax in a double boiler.
Take off the heat and add in coconut oil and honey (if using), allow to cook slightly.
Slowly pour oil over water and use stick blender to whip up.
Add essential oil for fragrance.
Pour into jars and allow to cool.

name: Hot cross buns
description: Before we start I strongly recommend 2 x the recipe and freezing them if you don’t think you’ll eat all in one sitting. I promise you’ll be happy you did!
ingredients: 400ml milk, plus a little more for glazing
½ whole nutmeg grated / ½ tsp grated
50g golden caster sugar, plus extra to glaze
instructions: Gently heat the milk in a saucepan with the spices, except for the ginger. Leave to infuse for at least one hour. Then strain and bring up to blood temperature (~36C) and mix with the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar.
Mix flour and cubed butter in kitchen mixer until resembling breadcrumbs. Add the  sugar and ginger.
Beat 4 eggs together. Make a well in the centre of the dry mixture and add the eggs and milk mixture.
Put in a lightly oiled bowl and cover with beeswax paper or a dampened tea towel. Leave to rise in a warm place until it has doubled in size. This typically takes a couple of hours.

Clean a large surface area and put some oil on it, you may need to add oil as you go to prevent it sticking.  Gently take the dough from the bowl. Create a stretched star-like shape and fold over each star triangle into the centre. Repeat if it wants more love. Pull and flatten the dough.
Sprinkle the dried fruit on the dough and fold it in energetically by stretching the dough.

Divide the dough into 32 buns; mould them them by stretching the dough as much as possible. Place them on parchment lined baking trays. Set aside in a warm humid area for the second proof. Wait until the buns double in size.
To make the cross lines on the buns mix the flour with the orange blossom water and add enough water to all you to roll the mixture with your hands. Set aside with buns while proofing.
Preheat the oven to 200°C / 390°F.

Roll the lines to fit across all buns. Lightly beat the remaining egg with a fork and paint the buns. Then assemble the lines. Apply a final paint of egg and put in the oven for 20-25 mins until golden brown.

name: Irish Spiced Beef
ingredients: 1 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme or ½ teaspoon dried thyme
instructions: 1. Start by placing the silverside in a good-sized saucepan. Add the salt, brown sugar, saltpetre and water. Bring to the boil and continue to boil for ten minutes. Allow to cool.
2. Leave the meat in the pickle for 5-6 days in the fridge. Turn it each day.
3. Remove from the pickle and drain.
4. In a bowl, mix all the spices well together plus the bay leaves and onion. Rub the mixture into the meat. Return to the fridge for 3-4 days, turning and rubbing daily.
5. To Cook: Put the meat in the saucepan and barely cover with cold water. Place a tight lid on the saucepan and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat and cook for approximately 3½ hours.
6. For the last hour of cooking time, add the Guinness to the cooking liquid.
7. When the joint is cooked, allow to cool in the liquid. Wrap in foil and keep in the fridge until required. Best served with homemade brown bread.

name: Jerusalem Artichoke (Sunchoke) Soup
instructions: Peal the artichokes and cut them into chunks, put them in articulated water to stop them from browning.
Dice the potato and other vegetables.
Put the butter in a saucepan and melt it, then add all the vegetables and stock.
Cook until vegetables are tender and using a stick blender blend into a soup.
Grate over some nutmeg and season to taste.

name: Lasagna
instructions: Make the bolognese the day before (for full flavour) and prepare the pasta the same day, you can make them to size and leave them dry - you can also make them the next day if you wish. Make the bechamel sauce.
Choose your dish, pyrex or a ceramic casserole usually work well. Layer in the bolognese then pasta, then bechemel, then again. I like to have 3 layers of pasta at a minimum.
Layer on 1/2 of the the cheese.
Bake on a 180°C / 350°F oven for 40 minutes, add the cheese and bake for another 20 minutes.
Serve fresh and enjoy with a salad with basil leaves, olive oil and balsamic vinegar.

name: Liquid soap
description: Recipe variations: Great cleaning with good suds (Feb 2023) (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/Great%20cleaning%20with%20good%20suds%20(Feb%202023)%20f5e878926d404ccd9576af5a2936da5b.md), Idea for next time - [To be named] (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/Idea%20for%20next%20time%20-%20%5BTo%20be%20named%5D%20e6244fccdaf4474685f0a79b6b872366.md), Feb 2024: Versatile clean (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/Feb%202024%20Versatile%20clean%2042ce1b73ca31458ba9178a49d6c4b92e.md), Feb 2025: [To be named] (Database%20of%20recipe%20variations%200c81384fd07149a6ae81d541becbd1a0/Skin%20cream%20variations%2040ceecb99b844506a6cc7c96ab35ed0e/Feb%202025%20%5BTo%20be%20named%5D%201868f15790cc80609f3ad23de89a2f52.md)
instructions: Put oils into slow cooker on high to heat them up
Mix lye (KOH) into water and stir until all flakes are dissolved.
Change slow cooker to low heat and slowly pour in the lye and water solution.
Stir the oil and solution together.
When mixed use a stick blender to bring the mixture to trace. This can take from 10 - 20 mins. Do so slowly so as not to burn out the stick blender.
Put the lid on the slow cooker and leave to gently heat for 1 - 2 hours. Mix every 20-30 mins.
When the mixture resembles vasoline it is ready.
Liquify
Weigh out amount of soap mixture to dilute.
Calculate x1.6 times the weight of glycerine (at 20%) and distilled water (at 80%).
Put glycerine and water into a saucepan and bring to the boil.
Add the soap mixture to the boiling mixture and cover it with as much liquid as possible.
Cover and leave sit - mix every now and then.
When cool bring all the mixture to the boil again. Slowly mashing the lumps.
Do this over a period of 2 - 3 days until everything is dissolved.
Thicken
Guar guar should be 1% total liquid soap weight
Mix guar guar with glycerin approx 4% of total weight and leave sit
Slowly mix into liquid soap and gently heat to a max of 60 C. Mix until all combined.
Leave to cool.

name: Liver Parfait
ingredients: 1 medium brown onion, peeled and finely chopped
100-200ml cream (add as much that creates a light brown colour)
instructions: Soak chicken livers in tepid water with 1 teaspoon of salt for 1 hour to draw out some of the blood. Drain and pat dry. Puree in a food processor.
Cook off the onions and sauté with butter, bacon, thyme, sage, and bay leaf. Sauté for 4-6 minutes until the onions are soft. A little colour on the bottom of the pan is desirable at this stage.
Turn up the heat, add the mushrooms and fry for a few minutes allowing plenty of colour to form on the bottom of the pan. De-glaze with brandy and reduce until almost gone. Add port and reduce by ½.

Taste and then add cream. Bring to the boil and cook 2-3 minutes, and add seasoning. Remove from the heat, leave to cool and add the livers. Puree in the food processor and pulse until smoot. Cook in water bath in a jar until each jar reaches 65C.
Can be sealed with ½ gee ½ vegetable oil.

name: Lupini beans
description: ![CC85E498-665D-466E-A6AD-6A9B952EDB26.jpeg](lupini-beans/CC85E498-665D-466E-A6AD-6A9B952EDB26.jpeg)
instructions: Soak beans  for 24 hours, make sure the water covers the beans as they soak.
Simmer for 2 hours to cook beans. Then leave to cool.
Soak in cold water in a large container. Change water daily.
After 5 days test for bitterness. When no longer bitter move to the next step.
Put beans in briny (salt) water, leave for at least a week then enjoy.

name: Mandal bread
instructions: Melt butter and stir in sugar.
Add orange and lemon juice with vanilla essence to mixture.
Beat in egg.
Sift flour and baking powder into wet mixture.
Mix in nuts.
Put flour on big board and divide  dough into 3 good size balls. Take one ball on board and flatten with fingers and palm of your hand.
Sprinkle chocolate on each dough pancake, roll carefully to form a log.
Transfer to baking pan lined with baking paper. Flatten to desired shape.
Repeat with other dough balls.
Keep light on in oven and in centre rack at 160°C  / 325°F degrees for 25 - 30 mins.

name: Meringue
ingredients: 💡 Typically for 6 people I would double this recipe for Xmas
instructions: Whip egg till very stiff.
Add castor sugar.
Add icing sugar.
Cook for 1 hour at 120C or 2 hours at 100C.

name: Mince pies
description: ![mince-pies.png](mince-pies/mince-pies.png)
instructions: Roll out pastry until it is approximately 2 cm high, you can make it thinner if needed.
Using a large and small cookie cutter for each mince pie cut as many as required. Cover in beeswax paper and place in the fridge.
Mix fruit mince with chopped apple and whiskey/brandy.
Put large pastry circle on buttered cupcake tin and put large cookie cut circle in each holder.
Add 1 - 2 spoons of fruit mince mixture into each.
Brush bottom of each small circle and place on each pie. Then using a fork press down on the entire edge of each pie.
Leave to rest in the fridge for 30 mins.
Turn oven on at 220°C / 430°F.
Take pies out of the fridge and brush each one with egg, put in oven and bake for 15 - 20 mins until golden brown.

name: Mixed peel
instructions: Peel oranges keeping peaks in quarters.
Submerge in water and bring to to boil, let simmer for 10 mins and then discard the water. Do this three times to remove the bitterness from the peel.
Mix water to sugar at a 2:1 ratio. Bring to the boil to desolate the water.
Add softened orange peels into sugar syrup and simmer for 2 hours on a very low heat.
Remove peel from the water and cut peels into strips.
Place on a wire rack and leave until dry. (This takes a couple of days.)

name: Moussaka
ingredients: [Garlic Roast Tomatoes](garlic-roast-tomatoes) / 1 large tin of tomatoes
instructions: Mash the garlic with a motor and pestle. Heat your cast iron pot / Dutch oven on a low medium heat. Add the garlic with some oil.
Dice the onion and when the garlic has started to become fragrant add the onion.
Increase the to a medium heat and fry the onion until it is caramelised.
Add the meat and fry it until it is lightly browned.
Add the remaining ingredients

name: Nut bickies
description: So depending on the nuts you use you can change the name. One of our favourites are Macabickies with some Milkadamia coffee!
ingredients: 300g Butter (@Marc Who try changing this for oil)
1tsp Nut essence (best to use same nut but it’s not vital)
instructions: Add all dry ingredients together.
Using the flat beater on a medium speed add in chopped butter.
Add in flavourings including chocolate.
Divide into three logs and shape as you desire, I like simple square logs.
Refrigerate for minimum of 4 hours, or just freeze them until you want to use them.
Preheat the oven at 190°C / 375°F.
Using a sharp knife slice the log(s) and place on a baking tray on some parchment paper.
Bake for 10 - 20 mins until golden brown. I like to flip them half way through.

name: Nut milk
instructions: Put nuts in a bowl and cover with water. Leave for at least 24 hours.
Drain off water and put nuts through juicer.
Mix all nut extract in blender with 800 ml water.
Chill in the fridge.

name: Olivia’s Muesli
description: Test
instructions: Test

name: Pancakes
instructions: Sift flour into a bowl.
Add sugar. buttermilk, egg and butter.
Beat with a wooden spoon until batter is smooth.
Add blueberries and orange rind and stir to combine.
Pre-heat an oiled frying pan over a medium heat.
Cook pancakes one at a time by pouring about¼ cup of batter into the frying pan.
Cook pancakes for approximately 1-2 minutes or until bubbles appear in the
uncooked batter.
Then tum the pancake over and cook for a further 1-2 minutes or until golden. Enjoy immediately or keep warm in a pre-heated oven.

name: Rhubarb upside down cake
ingredients: 8 small apples1 bunch of rhubarb, or approximately 6-10 stalks
½ cup of packed coconut sugar
instructions: Make the brown butter in the pan you will be making the cake in.
To make brown butter you must stay at your stove because it is all about timing. It may look like nothing is happening and then oh dear – it’s burnt. So: DO! NOT! LEAVE!

Add 190 grams of cultured butter into the pan on low-medium heat, swirl to evenly coat the pan and using a spatula, scrape down the sides as it starts to bubble. It will reach a point where it looks like it’s going to bubble out of the pan. Turn off the heat and remove into a medium mixing bowl. Cool and set aside.

Take eight small organic apples (you can use tart varieties or sweet depending on your preference – I like ones with a little bite of sourness). Fresh is the key, as you don’t ever want to cook with a mealy apple. Peel and core. Into the pan place 90g of cultured butter on medium heat, then place the apples face down until evenly brown – depending on the apple size and variety, approximately five to seven minutes. Flip and keep on the heat for another three to five minutes. Remove to cool in a bowl and set aside.

Next, you’re on to the rhubarb. I started by trimming the stalks down roughly to fit the pan. Don’t worry if they are seemingly larger than the pan – go bigger not smaller as they will reduce down. Cook them in the same pan that you browned the apples, making sure there is still butter left. Arrange the rhubarb so it covers the entire surface nicely. Cook it very briefly – just so the stalks are slightly softened to the touch (keep them intact). Remove them to cool into the bowl with the apples.
In the same pan, on low heat, add the packed organic coconut sugar, half a teaspoon of sea salt and two tablespoons of water, stirring until you’ve made a thick caramel. Let it cool and set aside.

Pulse the freshly shelled pistachio with buckwheat flour, baking powder, coconut flour, brown caster sugar, ground cinnamon, freshly grated nutmeg, one teaspoon of sea salt and blend until well incorporated.

Into the brown butter from the first step, beat in with a balloon whisk – one at a time – the duck eggs or hen’s eggs and one scraped vanilla seed pod. Continue to beat until it’s all well blended and looks smooth.
Add the dry flour mix and fold gently. It will look more like a bread consistency than a wet cake mix – do not worry, it will be fine.
Into the pan with the caramel, lovingly arrange first the semi-cooked rhubarb, then the apples, evenly around the pan.
Scrape the batter mix around the pan so that it coats the apples evenly and smooth the top of the cake.

Bake at 175°C for one hour, rotating the cake at 30 minutes to get an even colour. At the one-hour mark, turn off the gas and leave the cake in the oven for another 10 minutes. Take it out of the oven and cool for another 20 minutes.

ingredients: 220 g Oils (ideally with minimum of 50 g butter)
120 ml Water (must be distilled, rosewater, or equivalent)
instructions: Mix beeswax and hard oils into bain marie .
Mix remaining oils in a container.
Mix waters with aleo vera and vit E oil.
When hard oils have melted mix into the cool oils and mix well (you can use the stick blender or a spoon).
If using thickener add guar guar with glycerine and make a slurry, then slowly introduce the mixed waters until all incorporated.
**Wait** for oils to become translucent. **Observe** for when the centre is still runny and warm.
Use stick blender and mix oils together and slowly pour in the waters.
When all the water has been absorbed the mixture should resemble a cream.
Scoop into jars and ideally store in the fridge before using.
💡 If the mixture doesn’t blend into a cream put it all back in the bain marie (excluding any obvious waters) and put it over the heat. Use stick blender until it mixes into a cream.

name: Slow cooked beef
ingredients: Buy a 7lb bone 🍖 in first cut 3 bone standing rib roast (for 6 people)
instructions: Slice meat off of the bone. Salt with 2 tablespoons butter and kosher salt. Place meat back on rack. Let sit for up to three days in the fridge.
Cut slots on the fat cap cross hatch before you rub the salt on it.

When ready to cook. Put oven on at 95 C (200 F). Seer meat on all but the side that was attached to the bones until well browned. Let sit for ten minutes. Then tie the meat to the rack with butcher twine.
Roast meat 3-4 hours until it reaches 45 C (110 F). Turn off oven and let it sit 30-60 minutes more until it reaches 50 C (120 F) for rare.
Remove from oven. Let it sit at last 30 minutes. (I let it sit until I’m ready to serve). When ready to serve put it under the broiler for ten minutes to get the fat cap crunchy.

name: Sundried tomatoes
ingredients: Tomatoes: anything that will dehydrate in your climate, I’ve had great success with Siberian, San Marzanio, and even cherry (but fat cherry)!
Basil: if you start fresh you wil dry this anyway.
instructions: Slice the tomatoes in half so they dry as long strips as possible.

Lightly salt and leave to dry outside in the sun. This typically takes 3-4 days in full sun at 25°C / 77°F, if it’s 40°C / 100°F this will be less. You want them dry but not dried out and certainly not crispy.
If sun is not forthcoming you can put them in a fan forced oven low around 95°C / 200°F.
When they are dry sterilise enough jars for your tomatoes - I find a full tray will go into about a have that’s 250g / 1 cup.
Chop enough garlic for your taste and mix in enough basil to have a generous sprinkle on each tomato. Mix them all together with the tomatoes in a bowl.
Fill each jar with about 1/4 oil and then fill with the tomatoes. You need to press them down and make sure they are covered with oil. Use some toothpicks to hold them in the jar if necessary.
I find they need at least one month before eating.

name: Taco seasoning
instructions: Mix in spice grinder.

name: The 39ties
instructions: **Step 1** Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two nine inch round pans.

**Step 2** In a large bowl, stir together the sugar, flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Add the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla, mix for 2 minutes on medium speed of mixer. Stir in the boiling water last. Batter will be thin. Pour evenly into the prepared pans.
**Step 3** Bake 30 to 35 minutes in the preheated oven, until the cake tests done with a toothpick. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then remove to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Tiramisù
instructions: Carefully separate the egg white from the yolk. With the electric whisk, whisk the egg white with half the sugar, until the result is very firm, you almost can’t overheat these.
In a separate bowl mix in the yolk, and add the other half of the total amount of sugar.
As soon as it is ready it will be lighter and softer, then gradually add the mascarpone.
Continue stirring to obtain a thick and compact cream.
Now, gradually, spoon by spoon, fold the egg whites cream with the yolk cream, mix gently from bottom to top.
Once ready, take a large enough serving bowl and pour a first layer of cream.
Soak the ladyfingers for a few seconds, on both sides, in the already cold coffee, place them as a base.
Now add the cream again and then the ladyfingers, again the cream and garnish with the bitter cocoa on top.
Keep the tiramisu at least a couple of hours in the fridge before serving.
Enjoy your homemade Tiramisu!!! BUON APPETITO!

name: Trifle
instructions: Make [Sponge cake](sponge-cake) and leave cool.
Split the sponge and layer with strawberry/raspberry jam.
Pour sherry over.  Leave to stand.
Make [Egg custard](Egg%20custard%20f6af930d07414afd9a911a42c8f770a1.md) and pour it over the prepared sponge and allow to cool.
Cover with whipped cream.

name: Xmas Ham
instructions: Boil ham for 20 minutes to 450g (1lb) in water.
Glaze with cloves, brown sugar, and cider/lemonade placed on tray.
Cook for 20 minutes in the oven at 175C.

name: Xmas Ice-cream
instructions: Whip eggs whites into stiff peaks and add half of sweetener.
In separate large bowl whip cream thickly and add remainder of sugar/sweetener.
In the large bowl, fold both mixtures together with a fork or spatula.
Gently add fruit mixture, the cocoa or Baileys and toasted almonds.
Line a pudding basin with baking paper and add pudding mixture and freeze.
Remove from freezer 30 minutes before serving to soften, turn out onto a plate.
Serve with cream or a drizzle of chocolate topping.
💡 Can also be made into small molds or ramekins for individual serves

name: Xmas Turkey (or Goose)
instructions: Mix all brine ingredients together and put bird into a pot so the brine covers it entirely.
Leave to brine for minimum 24 hours.
Stuff bird with [Pork stuffing](Pork%20stuffing%204980fa39c0da449cb00dc2876b8706db.md) in main cavity.
Stuff bird with [Potato stuffing](Potato%20stuffing%20563f953235194d828c214fe79a95d227.md) in other cavity.
